We need to produce a test class that tests findLexicalRoot method. Need to set up JsonSchema instances with appropriate parent relationships and ids. The constructor is private; there is static factory method JsonSchema.from(...). But we can use reflection or mock? Since we cannot invoke private constructor directly. However we can use JsonSchema.from static method which returns JsonSchema given parameters. The static method signature: static JsonSchema from(ValidationContext validationContext, SchemaLocation schemaLocation, JsonNodePath evaluationPath, JsonNode schemaNode, JsonSchema parent, boolean suppressSubSchemaRetrieval);

We need to create a ValidationContext: requires JsonMetaSchema, JsonSchemaFactory, SchemaValidatorsConfig. We can mock these dependencies using Mockito.

Simplify: Use mock ValidationContext, mock SchemaLocation, mock JsonNodePath, mock JsonNode, and mock parent JsonSchema.

But findLexicalRoot uses getId() and getParentSchema(). Those methods are likely defined in BaseJsonValidator or JsonSchema. getParentSchema() returns parent field. We can construct JsonSchema objects using the static from method with real parent relationships.

But the static from method may rely on internal logic; but we can pass mocks for ValidationContext, SchemaLocation, JsonNodePath, JsonNode. The parent can be another JsonSchema created similarly. Should work.

Goal: test two scenarios:

1. When the schema has an id (non-null) -> findLexicalRoot returns itself (since while loop condition ancestor.getId() == null fails). So we need a schema with id not null. But getId() is derived from ValidationContext.resolveSchemaId(schemaNode) etc. Since we are mocking ValidationContext, we can stub resolveSchemaId to return a non-null id when called with schemaNode. However the constructor uses that to set id. But we are using static from, which will call the private constructor internally, which will call validationContext.resolveSchemaId(schemaNode). So we need to stub that method.

Thus we need to create a mock ValidationContext where resolveSchemaId returns "http://example.com/schema". Also need metaSchema etc. But we can also stub getMetaSchema, readAnchor, readDynamicAnchor to return null.

Simplify: Use Mockito to create mock ValidationContext, mock JsonMetaSchema, JsonSchemaFactory, etc.

But we also need JsonMetaSchema class; we can mock it as well.

Similarly, SchemaLocation may be used for id handling; we can provide a simple instance (new SchemaLocation(null, null)?) but its constructor requires AbsoluteIri and JsonNodePath. We can maybe mock SchemaLocation as well.

Simplify: Use Mockito to mock SchemaLocation, JsonNodePath, JsonNode.

Thus we can call JsonSchema.from(mockValidationContext, mockSchemaLocation, mockEvaluationPath, mockSchemaNode, parent, false);

But the private constructor expects schemaNode, etc. It will call super(...). BaseJsonValidator may require non-null parameters; but we are passing mocks, should be okay.

Thus we can create leaf schema (no parent) with id non-null. Then call findLexicalRoot and expect same instance.

2. When schema has no id (null) and has parent chain where ancestor has id. Then findLexicalRoot should climb up to ancestor with id. So we need child schema with id null, parent with id non-null. To achieve id null, we need ValidationContext.resolveSchemaId to return null for child's schemaNode. For parent, return non-null.

Thus we need two ValidationContext mocks? The constructor uses same ValidationContext for both schemas (likely same). So we can stub resolveSchemaId to return null for first node and non-null for second node based on node identity. Use when(mockValidationContext.resolveSchemaId(eq(childNode))).thenReturn(null); when(...parentNode...).thenReturn("id").

Thus we need two mock JsonNode objects.

Then create parent schema with parent null, then child schema with parent = parent schema.

Call child.findLexicalRoot() should return parent.

Also test case where there is no parent (null) and id null; while loop will break when getParentSchema null, return ancestor (which is child). So findLexicalRoot returns itself.

Thus three tests.

Thus test class can call JsonSchema.from.

@BeforeEach:
- mockMetaSchema = mock(JsonMetaSchema.class);
- mockFactory = mock(JsonSchemaFactory.class);
- config = new SchemaValidatorsConfig(); // real
- validationContext = mock(ValidationContext.class);
- when(validationContext.getMetaSchema()).thenReturn(mockMetaSchema);
- when(validationContext.getSchemaResources()).thenReturn(new ConcurrentHashMap<>());
- when(validationContext.getDynamicAnchors()).thenReturn(new ConcurrentHashMap<>());
- when(validationContext.getSchemaReferences()).thenReturn(new ConcurrentHashMap<>());
- when(validationContext.getJsonSchemaFactory()).thenReturn(mockFactory); // maybe not needed.

- also stub metaSchema.readAnchor and readDynamicAnchor to return null: when(mockMetaSchema.readAnchor(any())).thenReturn(null); when(mockMetaSchema.readDynamicAnchor(any())).thenReturn(null);

Now for each test we need specific resolveSchemaId behavior. Could set inside test using when(validationContext.resolveSchemaId(node)).thenReturn(...).

Now create SchemaLocation mock: mock(SchemaLocation.class). For its methods used: getAbsoluteIri, toString maybe; but not needed for id handling if id is null.

But the constructor uses schemaLocation != null ? schemaLocation.toString() : id. So toString may be called; we can stub toString to return "location". Use when(mockSchemaLocation.toString()).thenReturn("location").

Also schemaLocation.getAbsoluteIri() may be called; stub to return null.

Thus:

when(mockSchemaLocation.getAbsoluteIri()).thenReturn(null);

Now evaluationPath mock: mock(JsonNodePath.class); stub toString maybe not needed.

Now create schemas.

Parent schema: JsonSchema parent = JsonSchema.from(validationContext, mockSchemaLocation, mockEvaluationPath, parentNode, null, false);

Child schema: JsonSchema child = JsonSchema.from(validationContext, mockSchemaLocation, mockEvaluationPath, childNode, parent, false);

Now call child.findLexicalRoot().

Now verify result.

Write assertions.

Edge cases: findLexicalRoot uses getId() which may be null for child if resolveSchemaId returned null; for parent non-null.

Thus test passes.

Add @Test methods: testFindLexicalRootWhenIdPresentReturnsSelf, testFindLexicalRoot climbsToAncestorWithId, testFindLexicalRootWhenNoIdAndNoParentReturnsSelf.

Implement using assertSame.
